title: Squaring Up by Selection: NP-Completeness at Three Simple Roots
summary: To solve an overdetermined polynomial system numerically, one first makes it square, usually by replacing the given equations with as many random linear combinations as there are unknowns. This is a provably safe step, but it can substantially enlarge the supports. The alternative is to keep that many of the given equations themselves. Selection preserves sparsity but risks geometry: a genuine solution can cease to be an isolated point of the subsystem's zero set.
